params.requirement: The one mind of a general-purpose agent: it reads a conversation, plans, calls tools over several steps, reads their results and answers when the work is done. It needs dependable native tool calling, sound multi-step reasoning and a long context; a caller waits on every turn, so a reply should start within seconds and the price per call should stay moderate.

model.description: Provider model id of the agent's one brain. The template carries ctx.model (strict, resolved at instantiation); pass a RESOLVED literal (K-H2). The shipped timeouts are derived from the row named in `external_timeout_ms_row`; a model on another row derives them again from that row.

api_key.description: Provider API key. Deprecated, removed in 0.63.0: name a grant in credential_grant_id instead (#801).

credential_grant_id.description: GH #560: the grant this brain presents to get its bearer credential sealed from the agent's own `./access`, instead of carrying it in `api_key`. The template seeds it (`grant:openrouter@template-simple-agent/brain`), so the credential deposited as `cred:openrouter` reaches the brain over the credential v-lane, is opened in this task's RAM and is written nowhere. Which credential it opens is named by the grant, never here (R-AC-2).

credential_wait_ms.description: GH #457: how long one sealed credential round may take before every parked turn gets its `credential_pending` receipt. The substrate default is 10 s, which was measured against a broker standing beside the consumer; a member's broker is three python cells and two store round trips away from a brain four levels down, so this template ships the longer one. It bounds nothing but the WAIT -- no provider is called and nothing is billed while it runs.

external_timeout_ms_row.description: GH #1097: not read by the cell -- the catalogue row its `external_timeout_ms` and `cell.message_timeout` are derived from (the timeout chain, docs/cell-types.md § llm): the row of the model this cell is born on. A manifest that bears it on another row derives both again from that row.

reasoning_effort.description: GH #1300: how long the model deliberates before it answers, in the provider's shorthand (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `none` = off, or the lowest effort a model that cannot switch thinking off takes; passed through, not checked against a list). It ships `medium`, the effort every shipped llm cell runs at unless its instance says otherwise: an instance sets it through `override_params` on this cell's path, and a registry push that names no effort resets it to this birth value. On the chat-completions wire it goes out as `"reasoning": {"effort": ...}` (default `reasoning_wire`), on the Anthropic Messages wire as `output_config.effort`; `none` switches thinking off in the form the model takes. A `reasoning` object, where one is set, outranks it; a model whose catalogue `supported_params` omits the field never receives it.

description.purpose: The one brain of the agent: one llm cell, one model.
description.use_when: Inside the simple-agent template; the curator hands it the window, the menu rides in its tools.
description.not_in_scope: No second model, no thinking default, no model switch per call.
description.emits_meaning: the model's answer; tool calls go to the splitter and the dispatcher.
description.consumes_meaning: the curator's window and system slots.
examples: a turn -> tool calls -> their results -> the next call with iter+1 -> a text answer
